# Changing Text and HTML

#### Course: Make Your Website Interactive with JavaScript

## Changing Text and HTML

You have selected the element. Now, let's change what is inside it.

There are two ways to do that. And knowing the difference matters.

- textContent
- innerHTML

Let's see them side by side.

```html
1<!DOCTYPE html>
2<html lang="en">
3<head>
4  <meta charset="UTF-8" />
5  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
6  <title>Changing Content</title>
7  <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css" />
8</head>
9<body>
10
11  <h1>Changing Content Example</h1>
12
13  <p id="text-demo">(text)</p>
14  <p id="html-demo">(html)</p>
15
16  <script src="script.js"></script>
17</body>
18</html>
```

```css
1body {
2  font-family: sans-serif;
3  padding: 20px;
4}
5
6h1 {
7  margin-bottom: 20px;
8}
9
10p {
11  font-size: 18px;
12  margin-bottom: 10px;
13}
```

```javascript
1var textEl = document.querySelector('#text-demo');
2var htmlEl = document.querySelector('#html-demo');
3
4if (textEl) {
5  textEl.textContent = 'This is plain text';
6}
7
8if (htmlEl) {
9  htmlEl.innerHTML = 'This has <strong>bold</strong> text';
10}
```

Click Run Code.

The first paragraph shows plain text. The second paragraph shows bold formatting. Same pattern, different result.

Here is why.

- textContent treats everything as text.
- innerHTML treats the value as HTML.

![Idea Emoji](data:image/png;base64,)

Most of the time, textContent is the better and safer choice.
